span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the lower bound of the power-law range is chosen by minimising the Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance between the empirical distribution and the best-fit model above that bound - too high a bound shrinks the data and too low a one includes non-power-law points, so the minimum lies between
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: each synthetic data set is scored against ITS OWN best-fit power law rather than against the distribution it was drawn from, which is what makes the resulting p-value unbiased: the synthetic sets undergo exactly the calculation the real data underwent, fitting included
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: synthetic data are generated semiparametrically - drawn from the fitted power law with probability equal to the observed tail fraction, and otherwise resampled from the observed points below the cut-off - so the synthetic sets share the empirical body while following the power law in the tail
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the test distribution is constructed to be hard rather than convenient: it is exponential below the cut-off and a power law above, and its slope is CONTINUOUS at the cut-off, so it deviates only gently from the power law below that point - the authors' word is challenging
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: uncertainty on the fitted parameters is obtained by a nonparametric bootstrap - drawing a fresh sequence of n points uniformly at random from the original data and re-estimating both the lower bound and the scaling parameter on each surrogate set
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the alternative goodness-of-fit statistics are tested rather than assumed: reweighted KS and Kuiper behave like plain KS, while Anderson-Darling returns cut-offs an order of magnitude too large, and the cost of that conservatism is stated as fewer tail observations, larger error on the scaling parameter and less ability to validate the model
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the number of synthetic data sets is fixed by the precision wanted in the p-value rather than by convention, derived from the test's expected worst-case performance
span.note: about this quote: Q-607, 2026-08-16: THIS QUOTE IS TRUNCATED BECAUSE THE FORMULA IT LEADS TO IS UNREADABLE IN THE STAGED TEXT. The pdftext extraction flattens the expression for the required number of synthetic data sets out of order - the staged body reads 'at least 1 2 synthetic data sets' with '4 e-' appearing separately - so the rule the sentence states cannot be quoted verbatim without quoting nonsense. The span stops at the last readable words. The paper's own worked example (accuracy to two decimal digits requiring about 2500 sets) is likewise in the damaged region and is deliberately NOT reproduced here, because I would be typing it rather than cutting it.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the direction of the p-value is inverted relative to its ordinary use: the quantity being tested is the model the authors want to assess rather than a null, so a HIGH p-value is the favourable one and a low value rules the power law out
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: one can never confirm a power law, only find data consistent with it
span.note: what this limits: every power-law claim anywhere: Quotation withheld - the hypothesis cannot be confirmed
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: few empirical phenomena obey power laws across the whole range of x
span.note: what this limits: the range over which any fitted power law holds: Quotation withheld
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Known sampling biases in several of the reanalysed data sets were left uncorrected.
span.note: what this limits: the reanalyses in this paper: WE HAVE NOT ATTEMPTED TO CORRECT ANY BIASES IN OUR ANALYSIS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Many of the reanalysed data sets are partial samples of larger populations.
span.note: what this limits: the datasets reanalysed: MANY OF THESE DATA SETS ARE ONLY SUBSETS OF MUCH LARGER ENTITIES (SUCH AS THE WEB SITES, WHICH ARE ONLY A SMALL FRACTION OF THE ENTIRE WEB)
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The framework is presented only for the power law; no extension to other distributional forms is given.
span.note: what this limits: the applicability of the framework: IT COULD ALSO BE EXTENDED TO OTHER, NON-POWER-LAW DISTRIBUTIONS ... ALTHOUGH WE HAVE NOT GIVEN SUCH AN EXTENSION HERE
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The procedure often cannot separate power-law from log-normal behaviour.
span.note: what this limits: any claim that a power law rather than a log-normal has been found: IT IS EXTREMELY DIFFICULT TO TELL THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN LOG-NORMAL AND POWER-LAW BEHAVIOR
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Two model forms indistinguishable on the observed data can give enormously different extrapolations into the tail, which is where such fits are usually applied.
span.note: what this limits: extrapolating any of these fits to large rare events: the paper states conclusions from different fitted forms can differ enormously while being indistinguishable on the data
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Seven of the twenty-four data sets previously conjectured to be power laws are firmly ruled out.
span.note: what this limits: any of the seven named data sets as power-law distributed: HTTP connections, earthquakes, web links, fires, wealth, web hits and the metabolic network are ruled out here
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Two published scaling parameters for the same citation data disagree with each other and with this paper's maximum-likelihood estimate.
span.note: what this limits: a published scaling exponent for a data set: for these citation data three different values are in print, and the paper says the earlier two are incompatible with the maximum-likelihood estimate
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The accept/reject verdict rests on a stated p-value threshold of 0.1.
span.note: what this limits: the power-law verdicts in this paper: they follow a p-value threshold of 0.1, and cases near it are decided by that choice
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The range fitted is chosen, and that choice controls how much data the test sees.
span.note: what this limits: the sample size behind any of these fits: xmin is estimated, and it determines how many points enter the test
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Errors run in both directions on small samples: a power law can look like a good fit to non-power-law data, and true power laws cannot be separated from alternatives.
span.note: what this limits: a power-law fit on a small sample in either direction: the paper states both false acceptance and failure to discriminate occur there
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the fitting procedure is deliberately applied across twenty-four data sets from unrelated branches of enquiry, so that the method rather than any one field's data is what is tested
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a goodness-of-fit p-value computed for the power law AND for each plausible competing distribution, and the two compared
span.note: eliminates: that the power law fits because heavy-tailed data fits almost any heavy-tailed form - a log-normal or a stretched exponential may fit as well or better, and only comparing them shows which
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: an explicit rejection rule fixed in advance: p greater than 0.1 keeps the power-law hypothesis, otherwise it is rejected
span.note: eliminates: that the decision to accept a power law is made after seeing how good the fit looks
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the whole procedure was run on SYNTHETIC data drawn from known distributions
span.note: eliminates: that the method itself is wrong - synthetic data has a known answer, so the procedure can be checked against ground truth before it is trusted on real data
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
